Prove this Lean 4 theorem (source: FATE-M, difficulty: easy).

Informal statement:
A field, viewed as a ring, has only two ideals: the zero ideal and the whole ring.

Formal statement to prove:
theorem fatem_020_field_ideal_eq_bot_or_top {F : Type*} [Field F] (I : Ideal F) :
    I = 0 ∨ I = ⊤

Hand off only when the receiving role can act on concrete mathematical, compiler, or review evidence. A non-linear route is allowed, but extra communication is not itself success. The final proof must compile, preserve the exact statement, and contain no sorry, admit, or added axiom.

{"code":"import Mathlib

theorem fatem_020_field_ideal_eq_bot_or_top {F : Type*} [Field F] (I : Ideal F) :
    I = 0 ∨ I = ⊤ := by
  by_cases h : I = 0
  · exact Or.inl h
  · -- Case: I ≠ 0
    -- There exists a non-zero element in I
    have h_exists : ∃ x : F, x ∈ I ∧ x ≠ 0 := by
      -- Use the fact that I ≠ 0 implies there is some element not equal to 0
      have h_ne_bot : I ≠ ⊥ := by simpa using h
      -- Use Ideal.exists_ne_zero if available, or construct it
      exact Ideal.exists_ne_zero h_ne_bot
    obtain ⟨x, hx_mem, hx_ne_zero⟩ := h_exists
    -- In a field, non-zero elements are units
    have hx_unit : IsUnit x := by
      rw [isUnit_iff_ne_zero]
      exact hx_ne_zero
    -- If an ideal contains a unit, it is the top ideal
    have h_top : I = ⊤ := by
      -- span {x} = ⊤ because x is a unit
      have h_span : Ideal.span {x} = ⊤ := by
        rw [Ideal.span_singleton_eq_top]
        exact hx_unit
      -- span {x} ≤ I because x ∈ I
      have h_le : Ideal.span {x} ≤ I := by
        apply Ideal.span_le.mpr
        intro y hy
        simp at hy
        exact hx_mem
      -- Therefore ⊤ ≤ I, so I = ⊤
      rw [h_span] at h_le
      exact le_antisymm h_le (le_top)
    exact Or.inr h_top"}

        intro x

          simp at this
          exact this
        · intro hx
          simp at hx

      contradiction

    -- In a field, non-zero elements are units

      rw [isUnit_iff_ne_zero]
